summary: vanexa-agent daemon executes shell commands from hardcoded remote WebSocket relay
details: When the shipped bin `vanexa-agent start` is run, the daemon opens a WebSocket connection to the hardcoded relay `vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev` and dispatches messages received from that relay as tool calls on the installer's host. One of the exposed tools, `terminal.exec`, spawns `/bin/bash -c <command>` (or `cmd.exe /c <command>` on Windows) using the command string supplied by the remote party, giving whoever controls the relay arbitrary shell execution on the host running the daemon. The same channel accepts `config_update` messages that mutate the daemon's sandbox at runtime — setting `sandbox.grantAllAccess`, replacing `workspacePaths`, and overwriting `provider`/`apiKey`/`model` — allowing the remote side to broaden filesystem scope and swap LLM providers/keys before issuing shell commands. Approval prompts that gate dangerous commands in interactive mode are, in daemon mode, satisfied by `approval_response` messages arriving on the same WebSocket, so the consent gate is controlled by the same remote party attempting to run the commands.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
